recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-18083 unless FM separately decides to harmonize the historical ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRefPeriod name/cardinality with ClaimResponse, which would be a distinct later issue.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FM change request asking to add a root-level in-effect/effective period element for preauthorization responses in ClaimResponse and ExplanationOfBenefit, in addition to per-item periods.
initial_application: The explicit historical application is commit afb5ec66f68641293bb7950b6e0eeb118fa1444a, whose message lists FHIR-18083 and whose ClaimResponse spreadsheet change added ClaimResponse.preAuthPeriod. ExplanationOfBenefit already carries the same root in-effect semantics in current source as ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRefPeriod.
additional_context: ClaimResponse and ExplanationOfBenefit are active approved resources in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issues FHIR-22662 and FHIR-40082 added item-level reviewOutcome.preAuthPeriod structures for ClaimResponse and ExplanationOfBenefit, and FHIR-32762 found those item-level periods addressed later date needs without requiring another change. Zulip discussion confirms the top-level period is the whole preauthorization validity period while item-level periods apply only to individual items.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current active source already contains root ClaimResponse.preAuthPeriod and root ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRefPeriod Period elements, plus later item-level reviewOutcome.preAuthPeriod elements and content references for lower item/detail/addItem levels.
